Subject: Post-call recap: Throughput & SLO qualification

Thanks again for taking the call this morning — really helpful to see FinEx's production profile. Quick recap and open items so we have alignment before we kick off a sizing benchmark:

Summary of what I captured from the call:
- Steady-state: ~50 QPS (user-facing requests)
- Peak bursts: up to ~420 QPS during market open surges
- Average tokens per request: ~320 tokens (range 100–1200 depending on report size)
- Concurrency target: 60 simultaneous active requests typical, spikes up to ~500 concurrent during peaks
- Streaming: ~20% of calls require streaming partial responses (preferred for large reports)
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile under 300ms for non-streaming responses; for streaming we discussed softer SLO (~500ms for first partial chunk)

Open questions / asks from our side before we size more precisely:
1) Can you confirm the tokens/request distribution (median, 90p)? A sample CSV helps — ideal with timestamps to correlate peaks.
2) Do peak bursts correlate with specific cron jobs or truly user-driven spikes? That affects batching strategies.
3) Any long-tail requests that exceed 1200 tokens we should know about?

Next steps I propose:
- You share the workload sample CSV (timestamp, tokens, request type) — Rafael will use this to produce a recommended capacity estimate and a bench plan.
- We run a 2-day synthetic benchmark simulating steady and peak periods (we'll provide test API keys and a small harness).
- If numbers align, we draft a dedicated capacity proposal (commit-based pricing) and timeline for a pilot.

Thanks — copying Rafael & Marissa to keep the infra and CS lanes coordinated.

Thanks, Neha — quick technical notes based on the summary. I started a back-of-envelope capacity calc so we have a starting point:

Assumptions from the call:
- Avg tokens/request = 320
- Steady QPS = 50
- Peak QPS = 420
- Token generation cost roughly proportional to tokens/sec; concurrency matters for throughput.

Simple conversion: tokens/sec = QPS * avg_tokens_per_request; for sizing we usually convert to sustained tokens/sec and then map to GPU throughput. For a rough steady-state profile (no streaming):
- Steady tokens/sec = 50 QPS * 320 tokens = 16,000 tokens/sec
- Peak tokens/sec = 420 QPS * 320 tokens = 134,400 tokens/sec

Those are large deltas — for peak/steady we need to decide whether you want reserved capacity sized for peak, or reserved for steady + burst capacity (burst capacity handled by hosted or autoscale). A few clarifying questions that change sizing significantly:
1) When you quote 420 QPS peak, how long do peaks last (seconds / minutes / hours)? If peaks are <5 minutes and infrequent, we can absorb with burst autoscaling. If sustained for >30m, we'll need provisioned capacity.
2) For streaming: streaming calls are cheaper in tokens/sec at initial chunk but increase sustained kernel occupancy because they hold connections open. Do streaming calls require low first-byte latency (i.e., must return first chunk <200ms)?
3) Concurrency: are the ~500 concurrent during peak active generation requests or mostly waiting on network/IO? If they're CPU/waiting heavy, they affect slot blocking differently.

If you can drop the sample CSV I can run it through our sizing script (rough GPU equivalence, suggested cluster size, expected 95p latency estimate per model variant) and attach a bench plan.

— Rafael

Neha/Rafael — attaching the workload sample (finex_workload_profile_q3.csv). Couple clarifications inline:
- Steady-state figure (50 QPS) is our global average during non-peak hours, typically 10:00–16:00 UTC.
- Peak: 420 QPS is observed in a 30–45 minute window at market open (08:30–09:15 local) on weekdays; there is also a secondary smaller peak ~200 QPS around midday.
- Token distribution: median ~280, 90th percentile ~780, 99th ~1,600. We get the long tail from consolidated report exports.
- Streaming: used by the analytics UI for large exports — first chunk should ideally be <300ms, subsequent chunks can stream over 2–10s. It's ~18–22% of calls by volume but represents higher resource holding time.
- Concurrency: peak concurrent active generation requests ~480 (these are active model generation tasks).

Attachments:
- finex_workload_profile_q3.csv (sampled log with timestamps, tokens, request_type)
- I've also added a short doc with our target latency SLA language — finex_latency_slo.docx (please review).

Happy to hop on a quick 30m call if you want to sync on sizing assumptions — otherwise Rafael, please proceed with the sizing script.

Thanks,

- Redwood to provision temporary test keys + a small runner for a 48-hour benchmark simulating two windows: steady (50 QPS) and peak ramp (simulate 3 peak bursts to 420 QPS).
- After bench, we'll share a commit-sized Dedicated proposal + optional burst strategy (hosted fallback).
- Legal/PO: if the bench aligns, Marissa will scope the commercial proposal and draft the PO/contract language.

Can we tentatively schedule the benchmark for Wed 29 Sep — Thu 30 Sep? John, please confirm availability and any blackout dates. Also confirm whether FinEx wants the pilot in us-west region (we typically run bench in us-west for lowest network variance).
